answer: Cross-epoch linkage scoring names the mechanism. Each identity’s actions are hashed with a pearl carried into the next epoch as a continuity seed, so a fresh identity cannot inherit prior behaviour without replaying the whole chain. The rule enforces a relic of past interactions: reward accrual requires matching the prior epoch’s consistency key, and any mismatch resets accumulated standing. An attacker must therefore farm a comet of ordinary activity across every epoch for each clone, paying the full per-identity compute and latency cost repeatedly instead of minting cheap fresh keys.
